📚 DAILY MARKET EDUCATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📊 VWAP TRADING — Your Institutional Anchor

VWAP (Volume Weighted Average Price) shows where the smart money is positioned. Think of it as the fair value line institutions use to measure execution quality.

How it works:
- Calculated from session open using price and volume
- Resets daily at market open (00:00 GMT for forex)
- Price above VWAP = bullish control
- Price below VWAP = bearish control

Real example: EUR/USD opened at 1.0850 yesterday. VWAP tracked to 1.0865 by London session. Price kept bouncing off VWAP as support — classic institutional buying zone. When price finally broke below at New York open, the move accelerated 45 pips lower.

Trading applications:
- Use VWAP as dynamic support/resistance
- Fade extremes back to VWAP in ranging markets
- Trade breakouts when price commits away from VWAP
- Combine with session highs/lows for entries

PRO TIP: Major pairs respect VWAP more during liquid sessions (London/NY overlap). On GBP/JPY or AUD/NZD crosses, VWAP works best as a trend filter rather than exact entry level.

💱 CURRENCY INTERVENTION — When Central Banks Strike

Currency intervention happens when central banks directly buy or sell their currency to influence exchange rates. This is the heavy artillery of monetary policy.

Why they intervene:
- Currency too strong (hurts exports)
- Currency too weak (imports inflation)
- Excessive volatility threatens stability
- Speculative attacks need defending

Recent context: The Japanese Ministry of Finance intervened in USD/JPY multiple times when it breached 152.00 in recent years. Typical pattern — sudden 300-400 pip reversals within minutes, usually during thin Asian hours for maximum impact.

Warning signs to watch:
- Verbal intervention first (officials comment on FX levels)
- Currency at multi-year extremes
- Rapid appreciation (over 5 percent in weeks)
- Government statements about monitoring markets

How to trade around it:
- Reduce position size near intervention zones
- Tighten stops on extended moves
- Watch for unusual price action in thin liquidity
- USD/CHF and EUR/CHF particularly sensitive (SNB history)

SMART MONEY RULE: Never fight a central bank with unlimited ammunition. When intervention hits, exit first and analyze later.

🎯 THREE DAILY TRADING TIPS

1. CROSS PAIR OPPORTUNITIES
Major pairs choppy today? Check the crosses. AUD/CAD and EUR/GBP often trend cleanly when their USD pairs consolidate. Resource currency crosses (AUD/NZD, CAD/CHF) show clearer directional moves mid-week.

2. WEDNESDAY POSITIONING
Midweek typically sees the strongest directional moves. Monday/Tuesday build positions, Wednesday commits capital. If EUR/CHF or GBP/AUD broke key levels Tuesday close, expect follow-through today during European session.

3. VOLUME CONFIRMATION
Low volume breakouts fail. Before entering that USD/CAD breakout above 1.3650, check if volume supports the move. Thin volume + breakout = fade opportunity. Rising volume + breakout = genuine institutional flow.

🛡️ CAPITAL PRESERVATION — The Only Rule That Matters

You cannot trade your way out of a hole if you blow the account. Capital preservation beats profit hunting every single time.

The 2 percent hard rule:
- Never risk more than 2 percent per trade
- On 10,000 USD account = 200 USD max risk
- Hit three losses? You are down 6 percent, not 60 percent
- This keeps you in the game during rough patches

Position sizing reality check:
Trading GBP/USD with 50 pip stop? Calculate exact lot size to risk only 2 percent. Most blown accounts die from overleveraging one conviction trade, not from bad analysis.

The pullback protocol:
- Down 6 percent from peak? Cut risk to 1 percent per trade
- Down 10 percent? Stop trading, review every position
- Rebuild slowly with smaller size
- EUR/NZD might look perfect, but preservation trumps opportunity

Recovery math hurts:
- Lose 10 percent, need 11 percent to recover
- Lose 25 percent, need 33 percent to recover  
- Lose 50 percent, need 100 percent to recover

PRO TIP: Treat your account like institutional capital. A prop firm would pull your funding after 10 percent drawdown. Give yourself the same professional standard. Survive first, profit second.
